## AI that shows its work

Most AI tools give you answers and call it a day. FinMav shows you the filters, flags the gaps, and tells you when it had to make a judgment call — so you're in control of the screen, not just the recipient of one.

### Every filter, surfaced

Type a query in plain English and FinMav shows you the exact parameters it applied — P/E thresholds, EPS floors, debt ratios, yield ranges. You can verify, override, or refine. Nothing runs silently.

### Ambiguous terms get explained

When your query uses a term that could mean more than one thing — “quality companies,” “boring stocks,” “safe dividend payers” — FinMav tells you exactly how it interpreted it. No guessing what the model decided.

### Dropped constraints, not dropped on you

If a requirement can’t be enforced — say, “10 years of dividend growth” when that streak data isn’t available — FinMav surfaces an amber warning banner with a plain-English explanation. You know what was relaxed and why, before you make a decision.

### Screen Critic catches what you miss

Every screen runs through an automatic audit. Screen Critic flags value traps, sector overconcentration, contradictory filters, and thinly populated result sets — so you don’t walk into a bad screen with false confidence.

## Compare five stocks in one sentence.

Type “Compare JNJ, PG, KO, PEP, and VZ on dividends” and get a ranked five-column table broken down by yield, payout ratio, growth rate, and coverage — with the weakest and strongest performers clearly marked. No pivot tables. No copy-pasting from separate tabs.
